transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Marcus Hale (Sierra Medical Head of AI), Leah Ortiz (Security), Tom Nguyen (Infra), Aisha Reynolds (Compliance)

Summary (auto):
- Initial discovery focused on Sierra Medical's requirements for an on-prem, air-gapped deployment of Redwood Private.
- Key concerns: offline updates, hardware constraints (NVIDIA A100 availability vs older cards), key management for offline HSM/KMS, SOC2 / audit logs, model distribution process and validation, latency SLOs for real-time inference in clinical app.
- Next steps include sharing architecture doc, pricing/NDA, sample workload for benchmarking, and network diagram.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think everyone's on, um, thanks for taking time. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, AE. With me is Priya, our SE. You all good with quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus: Yeah hi, Marcus here, Head of AI at Sierra Medical. We build clinical decision support tools, mostly on-prem because of patient data regs.
[00:20] Leah: Leah, security engineer. I'm mainly focused on compliance and how anything on-prem fits our controls.
[00:25] Tom: Tom, infra. I run our GPU clusters and private datacenter ops.
[00:29] Aisha: Aisha, compliance. I'll be tracking SOC2, data residency rules.
[00:33] Priya: Great — quick agenda: 1) understand current infra and constraints, 2) map requirements to Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (on-prem / air-gapped), 3) talk update process and security, 4) next steps. Sound ok?
[00:43] Marcus: Yep, go for it.

[01:10] Priya: So to start, can you describe the existing infra for model serving? GPUs, networking, any air-gap requirements?
[01:18] Tom: Sure. We're in a colocation facility, we have mostly older cards — some V100s, a couple of A100s that are shared by other teams. For scale we'd probably want dedicated A100s or H100s but procurement lead time is long. And importantly — our environment is partially air-gapped: no outbound internet from the cluster that will run clinical models. Any software updates have to be vetted and pushed by our infra team.
[01:38] Marcus: And just to add, latency target is sub-200ms tail for the critical inference path in our triage UI. Throughput is modest, maybe 200–400 requests/minute but bursts happen.
[01:50] Leah: On the compliance side, we can't send PHI off-site. SOC2 and HIPAA are table stakes. Also need full audit logs and ability to prove model provenance.

[02:20] Priya: Okay, this is helpful. So conceptually Redwood has three options — Hosted API (we won't go through that because of PHI), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in our cloud) and Redwood Private which can be deployed in-customer — including an on-prem, air-gapped mode. For Sierra's constraints Private is the fit. Quick question on update cadence: how often do you expect model updates? Are you open to patch windows where infra team pushes signed images?
[02:45] Marcus: We're planning model refresh every 6–8 weeks, but security patches might be monthly. Updates have to go through change control; ideally we'd get signed artifact bundles that Tom can ingest and validate offline.
[02:58] Jordan: Right — we support an offline artifact flow. We produce signed deployment bundles, and customers can pull them into an internal registry or we can provide an encrypted USB image in extreme cases. It's called the air-gap image workflow, we do that for defense and pharma customers.
[03:13] Leah: Wait, encrypted USB — is that documented? We need chain-of-custody and verification steps.
[03:18] Priya: Yes, we have an onboarding playbook. We'll share a hardened runbook that describes signature verification using your HSM or a provided GPG key, checksums, and a verification step. It also documents rollback steps if a bundle fails validation.
[03:29] Aisha: Do you integrate with on-prem KMS or HSM? Keys can't be in a cloud KMS for us.
[03:34] Priya: Absolutely. We support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For air-gapped deployments we can integrate with an on-prem HSM via pkcs11 or an HSM gateway; alternatively you can use an offline hardware security module to unwrap keys locally.

[03:55] Tom: How does licensing and activation work when there's no outbound connection? We can't have the service phone home.
[04:02] Jordan: Good question. For Private we offer an offline license file mechanism. We generate a license tied to your hardware fingerprint; you can apply it via the admin console in an offline mode. Renewal can be done via signed tokens applied manually. We don't require continuous phoning home.
[04:18] Marcus: Timing — if we decide to go Private, what's a realistic pilot timeline given procurement of cards and your deployment support?
[04:25] Priya: If you have at least one A100 available we can do a small pilot in 2–4 weeks: install, test latency, run a canonical benchmark. If you need hardware procurement, we can run a remote benchmark using a Redwood Dedicated instance to set expectations while you procure.

[04:50] Leah: About telemetry — what telemetry does Redwood collect from Private instances? We need to be able to opt-out of any telemetry that might include PHI.
[04:58] Priya: Our Private agent defaults to local telemetry only. We can configure it to only emit anonymized metrics (CPU/GPU usage, token counts, error rates) and no request-level payloads. There's a config toggle during install; we'll include that in the playbook.

[05:18] Jordan: Are there any internal vendors you're evaluating? Marcus?
[05:22] Marcus: We're talking to Anthropic for hosted stuff and also looking at some in-house infra work. OpenAI was brought up but we can't use hosted for PHI. We're also evaluating Bedrock for managed options but it's not air-gapped.

[05:36] Priya: Understood. On the runtime side — can you tell us about model sizes you're targeting? 7B, 13B, 70B — and whether you'll prefer quantized int8 or full fp16/32?
[05:44] Marcus: Currently experimental models are 13B and 70B. For production we like 13B quantized to 4-bit for cost, but some research requires 70B fp16. Our infra team will need to know memory footprints to size nodes.
[05:58] Tom: Memory is the issue. Our V100s struggle with 70B. If we can't get enough A100s, is there a way to shard across nodes or use offload?
[06:07] Priya: The Redwood runtime supports model sharding and NVMe offload for KV cache in certain versions; performance tradeoffs depend on sequence length. We can provide guidance — for 70B fp16 you'd likely want H100 or multiple A100s or use quantized 4-bit to fit single A100 depending on sequence length. We'll share concrete memory profiles in the architecture doc.

[06:36] Marcus: For our critical path, we must keep p50 latency under 120ms and p99 under 200ms. That might rule out heavy offload.
[06:45] Priya: Noted — we'll include recommended hardware targets to hit those SLOs. It may mean reserving a few A100s per model variant and enabling batching config tuned for low tail latency.

[07:10] Leah: Encryption at rest — will Redwood write logs with PHI? How are logs stored and rotated?
[07:17] Jordan: By default Private stores logs locally and can be configured to redact request payloads. Audit logs for admin actions are maintained and can be shipped to your SIEM. All on-disk artifacts can be encrypted using your KMS.
[07:30] Aisha: For audit we need a tamper-evident trail — can you support write-once logs or signed audit events?
[07:36] Priya: We have integration patterns for signed audit events that are appended to your external log collector; in an air-gapped environment we can sign events locally and include an integrity verification step in the runbook. We'll include options in the playbook.

[08:05] Tom: Network topology question — do you expect the model servers to be in a separate VLAN? Any specific firewall ports?
[08:12] Priya: Typically we recommend isolating model serving in its own VLAN with restricted egress. Ports depend on admin console and runtime; for a minimal air-gapped setup, only internal ports are used and the admin console is reachable from a bastion host. We'll provide a network diagram and port list.

[08:40] Marcus: How do we validate model outputs during updates? We need a regression test harness tied to canary rollout.
[08:47] Priya: Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts for Private too. You can configure a canary percentage and associated eval runs. For air-gapped installs you can provide a test set and Redwood will run the eval locally and produce a report.
[09:00] Marcus: Good. Also, any mitigation if a model regresses? Auto-fallback?
[09:05] Priya: Yes, you can configure automatic rollback on regression thresholds and fallback to a previous pinned model. Policies are configurable in the private control plane.

[09:30] Leah: About supply chain — what's your SBOM story and third-party dependencies? We need to review packages that will be installed in our environment.
[09:37] Jordan: We produce a Software Bill of Materials for releases and can share CVE status and vulnerability reports. For air-gapped flows we also include the SBOM in the artifact bundle.

[09:55] Tom: Any special kernel or driver requirements? Our kernel versions are a bit old.
[09:59] Priya: We'll provide supported OS/kernel and driver matrix. Older kernels may work but we recommend RHEL 8 / Ubuntu 22.04 with NVIDIA driver 525+ for best perf; we'll note incompatibilities.

[10:20] Marcus: What about model provenance and reproducibility — we need to show which model version produced a prediction in case of audits.
[10:27] Priya: The runtime stamps requests with model version, artifact ID, commit hash and stores that in audit logs (configurable to avoid payload capture). That metadata is searchable via the local control plane.

[10:45] Aisha: Does Redwood provide SOC2 docs and penetration test reports?
[10:50] Jordan: We can share SOC2 Type II reports for Redwood cloud and a security guide for Private deployments. For penetration testing, we have red team reports and we can discuss scope and NDA to share sensitive docs.

[11:10] Leah: Can you map which parts of your platform would need external connectivity during install? We need to block anything that attempts DNS or package pulls.
[11:18] Priya: During the air-gap install all required packages are included in the bundle. There is an optional one-time staging step if you choose to pull from our registry — but for fully air-gapped we ship the bundle and there are no outbound calls. We'll detail the exact commands the installer runs.

[11:40] Marcus: For the benchmarking, can Redwood run the same model and workload in a dedicated instance so we can compare numbers before we have hardware on-site?
[11:48] Priya: Yes — we can spin up a Redwood Dedicated instance with the same model and run an identical benchmark harness and share the results. That helps calibrate expectations.

[12:05] Tom: About monitoring agents — can they be host-only? We don't want an agent sending raw requests out.
[12:11] Priya: Yes we can restrict to host-only metrics and only ship aggregated stats if you opt-in.

[12:30] Jordan: Any concerns on cost model — how are you budgeting for this?
[12:34] Marcus: We have capex for hardware and op-ex for software licenses. We expect a fixed private license fee plus support. Need a ballpark to justify procurement.

[12:45] Jordan: We'll include a pricing sheet for private deployments with monthly support tiers and optional uplift for air-gapped logistics. For procurement we can also offer pilot pricing to prove perf.

[13:05] Leah: Incident response — how would we coordinate if there's a security incident in the private instance?
[13:11] Priya: We have an incident playbook: if it's a Private instance, we work with designated contacts, share forensics artifacts (signed), and provide remediation steps. We can operate under your IR process and sign NDAs for sharing sensitive info.

[13:30] Marcus: Ok let's get into a few technical tradeoffs. For small models we might want to maximize concurrency; for big ones low latency. How does Redwood handle batching and KV cache policies?
[13:40] Priya: The runtime supports continuous batching with latency-aware strategies and an adaptive KV cache that keeps prefixes locally. You can tune batching windows and prefer low-latency paths. For high concurrency small models we tune batch sizes and parallelize across replicas.

[14:05] Tom: Is there support for quantization-aware kernels? Some earlier toolchains break accuracy.
[14:10] Priya: Yes, we've got quantization profiles validated on common model families; we'll share accuracy/latency tradeoff matrices. Some custom models require re-calibration.

[14:28] Marcus: We're also very sensitive to explainability logs — can we get per-request feature attributions stored without exposing PHI?
[14:35] Priya: We can log attribution metadata (vector of scores) without storing the raw prompt. That keeps observability while avoiding PHI.

[15:00] Leah: Are there known limitations in air-gapped mode? Any features disabled?
[15:05] Priya: Certain automations that rely on cloud (auto-scaling across regions, cloud storage plugins) are disabled. But core runtime, rollouts, monitoring (local), and evals run fine. We'll list feature flags in the playbook.

[15:30] Jordan: Quick check: what does success look like for you in a 3-month pilot? Marcus?
[15:36] Marcus: Low-latency production path validated on one clinical app, model accuracy not regressing vs baseline, and a clear runbook for updates that passes security review.
[15:44] Aisha: And compliance sign-off for SOC2 controls relevant to the deployment.

[16:00] Priya: Great. I'll quickly read back the main technical assumptions: 1) you will aim to provision at least one A100 for initial pilot, 2) model sizes targeted 13B quantized (prod) and 70B fp16 (research), 3) air-gapped update via signed artifact bundle, 4) telemetry disabled by default and logs redacted. Correct?
[16:20] Marcus: Correct, though procurement might push us to mixed A100/V100 for a bit.
[16:25] Priya: Ok we'll include guidance for mixed fleets but note perf impacts.

[16:40] Tom: For the offline license, is the activation tied to MAC addresses? We have changing hardware.
[16:47] Jordan: We prefer a hardware fingerprint that's flexible — e.g., set of host IDs or a license server within your network. We can work with your infra to choose a stable identifier.

[17:05] Leah: Can we do a security review call with your security team and our compliance folks?
[17:10] Jordan: Absolutely — we can schedule a vendor security review and share SOC2 artifacts under NDA. Priya, can you coordinate docs?
[17:16] Priya: Yes — I'll send the security pack and runbook.

[17:30] Marcus: Any references of similar deployments? Are there other healthcare customers?
[17:35] Jordan: We have a couple of regulated customers in pharma and med devices who ran air-gapped deployments — we can provide anonymized case studies and contact references under NDA.

[17:50] Priya: Quick note on performance validation — when you provide the sample workload please include sequence length distributions and tokenization details so we can reproduce.
[17:58] Marcus: Will do. We'll include a representative dataset (de-identified) and SLO targets.

[18:15] Tom: Regarding NVMe offload — have you seen acceptable p99s with offload enabled?
[18:20] Priya: It depends on seq length; for long contexts offload helps fit the model but p99 increases. For your p99 target we may recommend dedicating GPU memory rather than offload for the critical path.

[18:40] Aisha: For audits, we need to retain logs for 7 years. Is that configurable?
[18:46] Priya: Retention is configurable; we'll document retention and export options to your long-term archive.

[19:05] Marcus: Cost — any idea of uplift for air-gapped logistics?
[19:10] Jordan: There's typically a one-time onboarding fee for air-gapped support and an annual private license. We'll provide a breakdown but expect an uplift for shipping and manual artifact handling.

[19:30] Leah: On the SDLC side — do you support code signing for model artifacts? We sign our own models as part of provenance.
[19:36] Priya: Yes, we support verifying customer-signed models and will honor your signing pipeline; Redwood will verify signatures before deployment.

[19:50] Marcus: Any pitfalls customers run into with mixed GPU fleets?
[19:54] Priya: Main pitfalls are driver mismatches and uneven performance leading to noisy latency tails; better to size homogeneous pools for critical endpoints. We'll include a best-practice guide.

[20:12] Tom: For the admin console, is there an air-gapped UI or do you deploy a local control plane?
[20:18] Priya: There's a local control plane that runs in your network. It provides the same UI as hosted but all data stays on-prem. Admins access via internal network or bastion.

[20:35] Jordan: Okay we're getting close to time. Priya, can you summarize deliverables?
[20:40] Priya: Sure — I'll send: 1) on-prem deployment playbook and hardware sizing doc, 2) security pack (SOC2 summary, SBOM, runbook), 3) sample benchmarking template and checklist, 4) licensing and pricing sheet. I'll aim to send these by 2025-11-20.
[20:56] Jordan: I'll follow up with NDA and pilot pricing by 2025-11-21. Tom and Marcus — please share your network diagram and sample workload by 2025-11-25 and 2025-11-22 respectively.

[21:15] Marcus: Sounds good. One more question — do you support GPU pass-through in virtualized environments? We run some VMs for multi-tenancy.
[21:23] Priya: We support both containerized and VM deployments. GPU pass-through is supported; performance guidance will differ slightly.

[21:40] Leah: For identity, can we use SAML/AD and role-based access?
[21:45] Priya: Yes SAML SSO and AD integration for RBAC is supported for the local control plane. We'll include setup steps.

[22:05] Tom: If we want to do a quick smoke test before a full pilot, what's the minimal setup?
[22:11] Priya: Minimal is one A100 node, local control plane on the same VLAN, and a single model artifact. We can help with a one-day smoke test.

[22:30] Marcus: Great — that's probably what we'll start with.

[22:45] Jordan: Alright, any other blockers?
[22:48] Aisha: Need to review SOC2 docs first.
[22:50] Leah: Also need the SBOM and the installer commands so security can sign off.

[23:00] Jordan: We'll get those over. Thanks everyone.

[23:10] Priya: Closing notes: we'll schedule the security review and a benchmark run. I'll put proposed times in the follow-up email.

[23:25] Marcus: Thanks, appreciate it.
[23:30] Jordan: Thanks all. Bye.

[51:40] <end of recording>
